ResearchProjectDef.label: botania: mystic botany
ResearchProjectDef.description: Wild mystic flowers grow across the rim. Learning which ones hold mana, and how to plant them again, is where every Botania colony starts.

ResearchProjectDef.label: botania: mana
ResearchProjectDef.description: Study how certain flowers hold energy in their petals. Grinding them releases mana powder, which can be folded into steel or bound into wood, and stored in a pool of liquid light.

ResearchProjectDef.label: botania: generating flowers
ResearchProjectDef.description: Flowers that produce mana on their own. The endoflame burns fuel; the daybloom and nightshade simply drink the sun and the dark, then wither once their season is over.

ResearchProjectDef.label: botania: advanced flowers
ResearchProjectDef.description: Three flowers that ask for more than fuel: the furnace orchid feeds on a hot sealed room, the storm bloom salvages short-circuit bursts, and the rosa arcana takes what a mind has not finished learning.

ResearchProjectDef.label: botania: passive generating flowers
ResearchProjectDef.description: Flowers that pull mana out of daylight or moonlight without burning anything. Cheap and easy to place, but each one only lasts a season before withering away.

ResearchProjectDef.label: botania: garden craft
ResearchProjectDef.description: Bind livingwood and livingrock into a staff that can channel mana. This is where the wand of the forest is built; the petal apothecary comes later.

ResearchProjectDef.label: botania: functional flowers
ResearchProjectDef.description: Flowers that work for the colony instead of producing mana. The first of them is the thorn flower: a defensive bulb that slows anything hostile inside ten tiles, then bleeds it with mana.

ResearchProjectDef.label: botania: manasteel
ResearchProjectDef.description: Fold mana powder into steel to make manasteel: light, tough, and the skeleton of every advanced mana structure, from pools and relays to fluxfields and repairers.

ResearchProjectDef.label: botania: mana storage
ResearchProjectDef.description: Manasteel can hold far more mana than livingrock. A proper manasteel-lined pool keeps a colony's whole reserve in one place instead of spilling it across a dozen small bowls.

ResearchProjectDef.label: botania: mana mending
ResearchProjectDef.description: A bench that repairs gear with mana, and a tower that slowly mends walls and furniture. Both drain mana in proportion to the damage they undo.

ResearchProjectDef.label: botania: mana infusion
ResearchProjectDef.description: An infusion table that lets a colony craft high-tier goods out of mana instead of electricity.

ResearchProjectDef.label: botania: mana grid
ResearchProjectDef.description: Placeholder: relays with longer reach, bigger pools and a more efficient fluxfield. Content arrives in a later version.

ResearchProjectDef.label: botania: wand forms
ResearchProjectDef.description: Reforge the wand of the forest into two specialised forms. The sniper form trades rate of fire for one dense lance that punches through armour. The blast form throws slow, unstable bolts that burst into a cross of fire wherever they land, friend or foe. Neither form keeps the wand's plant-magic.

ResearchProjectDef.label: botania: alfheim gate
ResearchProjectDef.description: Placeholder: a gate that trades mana for elven materials. Content arrives in a later version.

ResearchProjectDef.label: botania: elementium
ResearchProjectDef.description: Placeholder: elementium weapons and armour. Content arrives in a later version.

ResearchProjectDef.label: botania: terrasteel
ResearchProjectDef.description: Placeholder: the terrestrial agglomeration platform, terrasteel and the Gaia ritual. Content arrives in a later version.

ResearchProjectDef.label: botania: gaia
ResearchProjectDef.description: Placeholder: unlocked by a gaia spirit techprint, not by points alone. Content arrives in a later version.
